You are LedgerLens, a financial research analyst. Answer strictly from the
numbered evidence. Every factual sentence must cite evidence like [E2]. Rules:
- Use only numbers that appear in the evidence or in calculate results; never estimate.
- Check the period carefully (fiscal year vs quarter, year-to-date vs single quarter).
- If the evidence does not support an answer (wrong company, period missing, metric not
  disclosed), refuse: say the filings do not provide it, and set "refused" to true.
- Be concise: lead with the direct answer in one or two sentences, then brief support.

Return JSON only, with these keys:
- "answer": text with [E#] citations
- "refused": true or false
- "value": the headline number exactly as written in your answer, or null
- "scale": one, thousand, million, billion or trillion (the scale of "value")
- "unit": USD, percent, ratio, per_share, shares, count or text
- "citations": list of {"ref": "E2", "quote": "short exact phrase copied from E2"}

Question: What was Coca-Cola's operating income for the three months ended October 2, 2026 (fiscal 2026 Q3), in US dollars?

Evidence:
[E1] KO 10-Q Q3 2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and | p.43
[KO 10-Q Q3 FY2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations > Operating Income and Operating Margin | pp.43-44]
* Calculation is not meaningful.

Three Months Ended October 2, 2026 versus Three Months Ended September 26, 2025

During the three months ended October 2, 2026, operating income was $4,465 million, compared to $3,982 million during the three months ended September 26, 2025, an increase of $483 million, or 12%. The increase was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 7%, favorable price/mix, lower commodity costs, lower other operating charges and a favorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 3%, partially offset by increased marketing spending and higher operating expenses.

Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, including the effects of our hedging activities, favorably impacted consolidated operating income by 3% due to a weaker U.S. dollar compared to certain foreign currencies, including the Mexican peso and Brazilian real, which had a favorable impact on our Latin America operating segment. The favorable impact of a weaker U.S. dollar compared to the currencies listed above was partially offset by the impact of a stronger U.S. dollar compared to certain

other foreign currencies, including the Japanese yen and euro, which had an unfavorable impact on our Asia Pacific and EMEA operating segments. Refer to the heading “Liquidity, Capital Resources and Financial Position — Foreign Exchange” below.

The EMEA operating segment reported operating income of $1,171 million and $1,097 million for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025, respectively. The increase in operating income was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 6%, favorable price/mix and lower commodity costs, partially offset by increased marketing spending and higher operating expenses.

Latin America reported operating income of $1,152 million and $897 million for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025, respectively. The increase in operating income was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 8%, favorable price/mix, lower commodity costs, lower operating expenses and a favorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 14%, partially offset by increased marketing spending.

[E2] KO 10-Q Q3 2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and | p.44
[KO 10-Q Q3 FY2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations > Operating Income and Operating Margin | p.44]
Operating income for North America for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025 was $1,766 million and $1,681 million, respectively. The increase in operating income was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 2%, favorable price/mix and decreased marketing spending partly due to timing, partially offset by higher commodity costs, higher operating expenses and higher other operating charges.

Asia Pacific’s operating income for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025 was $563 million and $521 million, respectively. The increase in operating income was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 8%, partially offset by unfavorable price/mix and an unfavorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 6%.

Bottling Investments’ operating income for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025 was $205 million and $57 million, respectively. The increase in operating income was primarily driven by an increase in unit case volume of 10%, favorable price/mix, lower commodity costs and lower operating expenses, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 2%.

Corporate’s operating loss for the three months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025 was $392 million and $271 million, respectively. This increase is primarily a result of higher annual incentive expense due to timing and increased marketing expenses, partially offset by lower other operating charges.

Nine Months Ended October 2, 2026 versus Nine Months Ended September 26, 2025

During the nine months ended October 2, 2026, operating income was $13,496 million, compared to $11,921 million during the nine months ended September 26, 2025, an increase of $1,575 million, or 13%. The increase was primarily driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 6%, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses, lower other operating charges and a favorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 4%, partially offset by higher commodity costs and increased marketing spending.

[E3] KO 10-Q Q3 2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and | p.40
[KO 10-Q Q3 FY2026 | Part I > Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations > Net Operating Revenues | p.40]
Three Months Ended October 2, 2026 versus Three Months Ended September 26, 2025

During the three months ended October 2, 2026, net operating revenues were $13,380 million, compared to $12,455 million during the three months ended September 26, 2025, an increase of $925 million, or 7%.

Corporate’s operating loss for the nine months ended October 2, 2026 and September 26, 2025 was $919 million and $994 million, respectively. This decrease is primarily a result of lower operating expenses due to lower annual incentive expense and lower other operating charges, partially offset by increased marketing expenses.

Based on current spot rates and our hedging coverage in place, we expect foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations will have a favorable impact on our full year 2026 operating income.
